design: Adversarial / minimax self-play against a market generator (robust RL): policy pi (per-asset daily weight vector) vs generator G emitting paths inside a plausibility set U (RARL knob adversary on drift/vol/corr; Wasserstein-DRO ball around the empirical panel; PAIRED-style regret with Bella as G; domain randomisation over Bella regimes). pi trained on max_pi min_{P in U} E_P[U(net PnL at fee16/slip5)]; the learned G then offered to Monte Carlo search as the leaf/rollout distribution ("patterns that serve Monte Carlo"). Attacked as a candidate SOURCE of a book clearing docs/pathway.md:9-21 (unseen years, PIT, 21 bp/side, >=3 seeds, beat +0.97 / PIT +0.56, hold positions, BEAR-positive).
lens: AMPLIFIER-NOT-SOURCE. A self-learning loop can only re-weight, sharpen or shrink the information already present in its training targets. Here the targets are (a) a fidelity/realism loss on the same Kraken OHLC panel a forecaster would see and (b) the policy's own PnL on generated paths. (a) is a function of the panel (data-processing: no more conditional-mean information than the best estimator fitted to the panel; the flow-matching objective weights the whole path law, so the daily drift channel — mean ~0.1%/day vs sd ~4%/day — is the least-identified part of it). (b) is information about pi, not about the market. Every literature number was re-read for gross-vs-net, in-sample-vs-OOS, and what "Sharpe" means; every repo receipt was re-read at file:line.
strongest_objection: The loop's fixed point is decided by whether the plausibility set contains a measure whose conditional drift is zero or reflected along the policy's positions — and every data-driven set does. Blanchet–Chen–Zhou Prop. 1 (arXiv 1802.04885, full text extracted and read): min_{P: W2(P,P_n)<=delta} E_P[phi^T R] = E_{P_n}[phi^T R] − sqrt(delta)·||phi||_p; Thm 1 turns robust mean–variance into min_phi (sqrt(phi^T Var phi) + sqrt(delta)||phi||_p)^2; §3.1 verbatim: "If δ is too large, then there is too much model ambiguity and the available data becomes less relevant. In this case the resulting optimal portfolios will tend to be just equal allocations"; delta_n should be O(n^-1), picked by RWPI at 95%. By Hölder, a cost-charged long-short book has robust EV <= (||mu_hat||_q − sqrt(delta))||phi||_p − cost·turnover, so the robust book is non-flat only in directions where the estimated drift exceeds the radius plus 21 bp of turnover — a t-statistic gate on a forecast, i.e. the memo's G-A instrument (lore/fable_direction_memo_2026-09-03.md:305-306) computed the expensive way. With daily conditional-mean IC ~0 (memo §1.3), mu_hat is inside any RWPI radius and pi* is flat (long-short) or 1/N (fully-invested): both already on record — flat = 887 A-arm 99.0% hold (experiments/LEDGER.md:97) and 812 100% HOLD OOS (lore/notes_2026-06-26.md:104-117); 1/N = PIT equal-weight gross −0.40 FULL / −2.54 BEAR22 / −0.29 BULL24 / −1.63 CHOP25 (runs/819_single_asset/POWERED_RESULT.md, "Market context" table; the column is a daily-rebalanced EW book, trader/backtest.py:225-227). The RARL analogue confirms robustness buys variance, never expectation: Spooner–Savani 2020 (arXiv 2003.01820, full text extracted) Thm 1 has the adversary set drift against inventory (b* = lower bound when H>0, upper when H<0), and Table 1a→1c reads terminal wealth 67.0±12.0 → 65.1±6.7, "Sharpe" 5.57 → 9.78, inventory 0.56±7.55 → −0.05±1.94 — the MEAN FELL; footnote 3 says that "Sharpe" is E[Pi_N]/sqrt(V[Pi_N]) on terminal wealth over 10^5 episodes, and every test episode was generated with the FIXED (nominal) adversary, so the robust agent was scored on the nominal world and still earned less on average; the paper itself warns inventory penalties yield "strategies that try to avoid trading at all, a frequent problem in this domain". Their agent kept a positive mean from spread capture; a daily spot taker book has no exogenous income, so its zero-inventory equilibrium is FLAT, whose bear PnL is 0, not positive. BEAR-positive therefore requires the set U to EXCLUDE bear-adverse drift, which is a bear forecast smuggled into the constraint. The Monte-Carlo-leaf use inherits the same bound and the record's leaf results: a G-rollout leaf is E_G[future PnL | state], a forecast under G with at most the panel's drift information; learned leaves are measured action-blind (849/leaf v-hat corr +0.03) and subtractive (879 delta 1.602), and the only leaf that ever scored (+8.02, E5-inversion3) was the TRUE 3-day path (831x/C: R1 +1.95 → R3 +5.29), which a causally-conditioned generator cannot emit by construction. Steelman considered and rejected: (i) the static-vs-dynamic gap — Bartl–Wiesel 2023 (SIAM J. Fin. Math., arXiv 2208.05656, abstract-level) give explicit first-order approximations of multiperiod values under adapted-Wasserstein perturbations, i.e. robust value = nominal − radius × a sensitivity norm, the same shape; a path-space adversary widens no-trade bands, it does not create drift; (ii) regime-robustness would have cut 875 f5's −33% PV drawdown — a variance/drawdown benefit at <=0 expectation; (iii) second-moment predictability (vol clustering) is real and a generator can carry it — that is sizing (tactics panel row 4, odds 1–2%), not expected return.
amplifier_check: Verdict: AMPLIFIER ONLY — and with respect to the conditional mean, an ATTENUATOR. The loop's two learned objects: (1) G_adv = argmin over U of pi's utility. Its targets are the panel (fidelity) and pi's loss (adversarial). The fidelity term cannot carry more conditional-mean information than a forecaster fitted to the same panel (data-processing inequality; and a generator trained on the whole path law identifies the drift channel worse than a regression aimed at it — the memo's own §5 point, lore/fable_direction_memo_2026-09-03.md:374-377). The adversarial term is information about WHERE PI IS FRAGILE, not about the market. (2) pi* = the minimax fixed point = a pessimism operator applied to the panel's drift: it removes every component of the estimated conditional mean below sqrt(delta) per unit position (Prop. 1), so the loop strictly attenuates the target signal before the policy sees it. Nothing in the loop injects information that is not in (panel, pi). Worth if daily IC ~0: alpha value exactly 0 — pi* is flat or 1/N, both measured negative-to-zero on PIT 2024–26; the G-leaf inside MCTS then supplies a zero-mean noisy value, and search selecting on noise buys turnover tax (831x/D: K16 +5.29 → K128 +4.68 monotone decline "extra candidates buy TURNOVER TAX, not alpha", experiments/LEDGER.md:53). Residual worth is a certificate about the policy class (already held empirically six ways), a stress distribution for R4 (docs/pathway.md:84-85, D5), and a shrinkage rule that is algebraically the G-A t-stat gate. Escape from 887/collapse-confirm: none inside the loop — minimax makes the adaptive abstention a theorem; the only mechanical escape is to shrink U until some phi clears radius+cost, which asserts a forecast with a confidence bound, i.e. the instrument outside the loop. The PAIRED variant additionally cannot escape regret saturation: regret = (optimal − actual)/|optimal| (diff_teacher/adversarial_training.py:355) against a perfect-foresight oracle (diff_teacher/optimal_solver.py:2-4) equals 1 for any HOLD policy on every path, so the generator's objective is flat in path structure; Dennis et al. 2020 (abstract, verbatim) "minimax adversarial training leads to worst-case environments that are often unsolvable" and regret must be against a trainable antagonist; and the trainer never updates G at all (adversarial_training.py:410-411 "TODO: Implement proper gradient-based update"; checkpoints/diff_teacher_adversarial is an empty directory; the only run is the 2-epoch metrics smoke, lore/notes_2026-01-24.md:1307-1333).

record_conflicts.receipt: Proposal kill_experiment.design: "U3 = U2 + global reflection of the market-residual return component ... includes the zero-drift measure by symmetry"; pass_fail P1: "P1 holding => any minimax loop whose plausibility set admits drift reflection outputs flat by construction; GPU version killed"
record_conflicts.conflict: The tactic library is dominated by sign rules that are ODD in returns: the 819 book is sign(logC_t − logC_{t−30}) equal-weight (trader/config.py:89-94), and the proposed 7d/21d reversal L/S books are −sign(past residual). Under global reflection r → −r (residual or total) positions flip together with forward returns, so PnL = pos·fwd is INVARIANT; reflection is a symmetry of autocorrelation-based tactics, not a zero-drift null for them. Likewise blockwise time-reversal preserves the autocovariance function of a stationary series (gamma(k) = gamma(−k)), so the linear trend/reversal premium survives to second order, and a 21-day date block bootstrap preserves ≤21-lag dependence, so the 7d reversal signal survives. Only static residual tilts (the beta-hedged mix) flip sign under U3; the EW constant mix has zero residual vs its own market and is untouched. P1 will still 'hold' on 2024–26, but because every tactic's bootstrap lower bound is < 0 on that window (a t-stat gate, already on record: 819 Phase 3 FULL net@21 +0.56 CI[−0.13,+1.23], POWERED_RESULT.md; 898 2024 CI[−1.99,+2.10], 2025 CI[−1.21,+2.36], 2026H1 CI[−5.30,+0.95], LEDGER.md:103) — NOT because of the minimax symmetry. Run the same design on 2021–2023 and U3 selects trend at ~+1.8. The inference 'GPU version killed by construction' would be a false generalisation from the wrong mechanism.

record_conflicts.receipt: Proposal kill_experiment.pass_fail P2 and honest_odds: "realised UNSEEN 2026H1 net@21 beats BOTH the nominal U0 choice and flat by more than the bootstrap CI half-width ... P(P2 PASS) ≈ 5-10%"
record_conflicts.conflict: experiments/LEDGER.md:103 (898/trend-decay) shows what a half-year CI looks like on this scorer: 2026H1 baseline −1.659 CI[−5.30,+0.95] (half-width ≈3.1), long-flat −5.221 CI[−7.89,−2.09] (half-width ≈2.9). P2 therefore requires a tactic to post net@21 ≳ +3 on six months to beat flat by a half-width — a 1-in-50-ish noise event for a genuinely null tactic and essentially unreachable for a real effect of the size the goalposts need (+0.97). The stated 5–10% is mis-calibrated in the wrong direction; a P2 FAIL is uninformative by construction.

record_conflicts.conflict: Verified verbatim in the extracted text, but the paper's footnote 3 defines it as E[Pi_N]/sqrt(V[Pi_N]) on TERMINAL WEALTH over 10^5 episodes ("While the Sharpe ratio would normally use returns, for our relative comparison of agents we use terminal wealth"), and Table 1's caption says every test episode was generated with the FIXED adversary. surviving_claim: As a SOURCE of edge the design is dead: P(minimax/adversarial self-play is the source of a book clearing the goalposts) ≈ 0–1%, and that residual is the probability that the plausibility set is tuned to leave a forecast in — which is the IC instrument by another name. What survives, all at +0 expected Sharpe and all downstream of a forecast that must be found first: (1) The DRO shrinkage rule as closed-form sizing inside the Gârleanu–Pedersen controller — trade only where mu_hat^T phi − sqrt(delta_n)||phi||_p − cost > 0 with delta_n = O(1/n) by RWPI at 95% (n ≈ 910 days on 2024-01→2026-06) — a paragraph of arithmetic on the G-A IC table, CPU, no loop, no GPU. (2) Bella as the R4 regime-stress GATE exactly as D5 and docs/pathway.md:84-85 already say, with its daily-bar fidelity measured first and its skeleton drift pinned to zero when used as a stress set. (3) A surrogate null family for the IC instrument — but NOT the U1–U3 family as specified; the null that actually destroys conditional-mean alignment while preserving marginals, vol clustering and cross-sectional covariance is the circular-shift / per-date-permutation placebo the tactics panel's row 3 already names (lore/fable_tactics_panel_2026-09-04.md:115-117). (4) A precise answer to the operator's question: the only 'pattern that serves Monte Carlo' is a conditional-mean forecast; a generator adds at most evaluation-variance reduction for comparing candidate books (common random numbers / control variates), never information — and at IC ~0 a generator leaf adds turnover tax (831x/D). (5) The honest 778 point: Bella-as-MCTS-rollouts has never been run, and the same information bound says it need not be — 831x/C locates the search value in a true 3-day lookahead a causal generator cannot supply. Record hygiene surviving from the proposal: TASK_110's banner "Phase 1-4 Complete" (tasks/TASK_110_ADVERSARIAL_MARKET_GENERATOR.md:3) is overstated — the generator update is a TODO (diff_teacher/adversarial_training.py:411) and the adversarial checkpoint directory is empty; the planner may correct it at disarm.
kill_experiment_critique: Do not run it as written; fold its one useful column into tactics panel row 1. Reasons: (1) It does not test the design — no adversary is trained, no policy is trained on the min, no G is offered to search — so neither P1 nor P2 can 'kill the GPU version' empirically; the kill is analytic (Prop. 1 + Hölder + the measured IC) and is already complete on paper, so the day of implementer time buys no information. (2) P1's mechanism is wrong: reflection is an exact invariance of sign-rule tactics (positions flip with returns), blockwise time-reversal preserves autocovariance, and a 21-day block bootstrap preserves the 7d reversal's dependence; U3 discriminates tactics by their algebraic parity (beta-hedged mix flips, EW mix untouched, sign rules invariant), not by edge. P1 will 'hold' on 2024–26 only because every tactic's bootstrap lower bound is already < 0 (POWERED_RESULT.md FULL CI[−0.13,+1.23]; LEDGER.md:103 2024/2025/2026H1 CIs span 0) — the generalisation to 'any minimax loop admitting drift reflection outputs flat by construction' would be false (on 2021–2023 U3 selects trend). (3) The 'robust selector = 10th percentile over surrogates' is a one-sided ~80% lower confidence bound; trader.backtest.cell_metrics already prints a 2000-resample block-bootstrap CI (trader/backtest.py:157, :231) and tactics row 1 already builds the same K≈8 library — so the whole experiment reduces to one extra printed column ('CI lo < 0 ⇒ robust-flat'). (4) P2 is power-starved: 2026H1 half-widths are ≈3 Sharpe units on this scorer (LEDGER.md:103), so 'beats flat by more than the half-width' needs net@21 ≳ +3 on six months; its stated 5–10% PASS odds are mis-calibrated and a FAIL is uninformative. (5) If a surrogate null is wanted for the IC instrument (memo E-2's replacement for the 819 CAPACITY max-of-four-shuffles floor), the correct family is the circular-shift placebo (shift signals relative to returns by k ≫ horizon) and per-date cross-sectional permutation of residual returns — these destroy conditional-mean alignment while preserving marginals, vol clustering and the market factor; U1–U3 do not. (6) The optional Bella U4 arm smuggles drift via the skeleton's trend_direction/alpha_shape knobs (diff_teacher/skeleton/types.py:35,50) unless pinned to zero, and Bella's daily-bar fidelity is unmeasured — any non-flat selection there is a skeleton artefact. (7) Cost check: 8 tactics × ~600 surrogates × cell_metrics with n_boot 2000 left on is ~4,800 cells × 2,000 resamples — hours, not 'minutes to ~1 hour'; the inner bootstrap is redundant with the surrogate percentile and should be disabled for surrogate cells. (8) The compute framing for the full loop leans on the 875 anchor, which is train+eval (LEDGER.md:99), inflating the GPU estimate ~10×; irrelevant to the verdict but should not enter lore. What to record instead, if closure is wanted: one line in the LEDGER pointing at Prop. 1 and the G-A gate, plus the DRO radius sqrt(delta_n) computed for n ≈ 910 and compared with ||mu_hat_resid||_q once the IC table exists — zero new code, zero GPU, and it hands the 64 GB cards to nothing in this family until G-A reports.
